correctness.rationale: A first-arrival calculation for the mixed-spider graph gives probability q_j=(ell+2j)/(2^k(ell+2j+1)) for each fixed noncenter independent set choosing j inner vertices. Relative to uniform 1/(2^k+1), its deviation is (ell+2j-2^k)/(2^k(2^k+1)(ell+2j+1)); center deviation is minus their sum. Total variation is max(P_ell,M_ell)/(2^k(2^k+1)), P strictly rising after positive terms and M strictly falling before vanishing. Binomial symmetry at ell0=2^k-k makes P-M negative and at ell0+1 positive; only those two integers can minimize (when ell0>=1). Exact small rational comparisons for k=1..6 decide exceptions, and 2^k+1>2k(k+1) for k>=7 gives ell0. The star k=0 is separately handled. At optimum, E|2J-k|~sqrt(2k/pi) proves bias ~sqrt(1/(2pi))*sqrt(k)/4^k. An independent exact-probability implementation checked 24 small cases and the optimizer at ten k values. Boundary k=1,2,3 explicitly included.
residual_risks: Optimizes ell>=1 at each fixed k; graph order changes with ell, not an optimum over trees at fixed order.
No claim of exact uniformity for k>=1; finite tests supplement analytical proof.

originality.rationale: Fairfax-Ball already derives the exact q_j law and evaluates/tunes ell=2^k-k to obtain only O(sqrt(k)/4^k). The primary source does not establish that ell is uniquely optimal over all positive integers, does not identify exceptional small k=1,3 choices or obtain the asymptotic lower leading constant. The optimization and sharp constant thus remain a nontrivial extension rather than reprinting the starting probability formula.
